title: Taking customers from Bookly and Amelia
subtitle: Compete mode, quick depth. 139 one-to-three-star WordPress.org reviews mined across Bookly, Amelia, BookingPress and LatePoint, plus vendor pricing pages. Every quote was re-checked by verify.py.

verdict.summary: The pain is real and recent, mostly with Amelia: updates break live bookings and support takes days to weeks. But well-rated LatePoint and SSA already catch switchers, and nobody has shown they'll pay a newcomer. Don't launch as booking plugin #785. Sell a done-for-you migration and rescue off Amelia/Bookly first, at $149, with your plugin as the destination. If 3 people pay within 7 days, re-score.

opportunities.name: Rescue & migration off Amelia/Bookly (service first, then importers in your plugin)
opportunities.one_liner: Fixed-price, done-for-you move off a broken Amelia or Bookly install, with a no-lost-appointments check.
opportunities.why: Business-stopping incidents (e18, e65) and lock-in (e46-e48) are real. Self-serve importers already exist (e84, e85, e86), so the offer is the labour and the guarantee. WTP is capped at 5: no evidence yet that anyone pays a third party to migrate. Cheap to build and fits 15 h/week.

opportunities.name: Developer-first, WordPress-native booking engine for freelancers and agencies
opportunities.one_liner: WP users, documented hooks, clean uninstall and a multi-site license for people who install booking on client sites.
opportunities.why: Developers complain about Amelia's separate user system, its own tables and missing hooks (e39-e41). Their clients phone them when booking breaks (e62, e63, e65). WP-native rivals exist: a reviewer switched to Fluent Booking (e56). The engine is a months-long build.

opportunities.name: Switch-in booking plugin for small salons and practitioners (the current plan, sharpened)
opportunities.one_liner: Import from Bookly/Amelia, rollback-safe updates, bookings that survive a lapsed license, developer support.
opportunities.why: Hits the top two themes (updates e10, e13; support e2, e4). But LatePoint (98/100, every feature at $79, e71/e72) and SSA (1-business-day support, e75) already serve unhappy switchers well. A one-day support promise is hard at 15 h/week.

gap.statement: Small appointment businesses on Bookly or Amelia, and the WordPress freelancers who set them up, can't get updates that don't break today's bookings or support that answers within a day, because both market leaders ship breaking updates behind slow ticket queues, and leaving means rebuilding customers, services and future appointments by hand.

pains.theme: Support is slow, scripted or absent
pains.summary: Tickets wait days to weeks while bookings are down; reviewers leave over it.

pains.theme: An update breaks live bookings or loses data
pains.summary: Lost appointments, wiped customers, payments with no booking. Recent for Amelia (2025-2026).

pains.theme: Lapsed license means no fixes, nags or a broken dashboard
pains.summary: Bookly support expiry called 'ransom'. Amelia renews at the full crossed-out price.

pains.theme: Basics locked behind add-ons or tiers
pains.summary: Historic Bookly complaint (2018-2023); Bookly now bundles tiers. Free versions called an 'advertisement'.

pains.theme: Scheduling logic doesn't fit service businesses
pains.summary: Idle gaps, forced employee step for solo shops, no multi-service front-desk booking, no multi-staff.
Separate user system, own tables, no hooks or docs, tables left after uninstall.
Hard to add a booking or client from the backend; a salon left in 2026 over it.

pains.theme: Locked in: data hard to get out, sunk license cost
pains.summary: Rare, but it's the barrier to every switch.
Marketplace refund rules used to refuse refunds.

competitors.name: Bookly
competitors.pricing: Pro $99/yr list ($39 on sale) or $129 lifetime ($99 on sale), 1 site; Business and Ultimate tiers above
weaknesses: 0 low-star reviews in the last 12 months in the sample, so a weaker target today

competitors.name: Amelia
competitors.pricing: 4 tiers; geo-based pricing (annual figures JS-rendered, not captured); renews at the full crossed-out price
competitors.positioning: No hidden costs or add-ons (pricing page); up to 40% off the first year
weaknesses: Support waits of days to weeks
No multi-service booking from the admin

competitors.name: LatePoint
competitors.pricing: Starter $99/yr list ($79 on sale), every feature on every plan; renewals at full price
competitors.positioning: Pricing that scales with your business.
strengths: Multiple agents on the entry plan
weaknesses: Google Calendar missing from free version

competitors.name: Simply Schedule Appointments
competitors.pricing: Plus $129/yr list ($99 sale); team scheduling only in Business $499 list ($399 sale)
competitors.positioning: Try it. Love it. Or get a full refund within 30-days, guaranteed!
weaknesses: Team scheduling gated to the top tier

competitors.name: BookingPress
competitors.positioning: The best WordPress booking plugin, at the best price.
strengths: Ships a Migration Addon (from Amelia, Bookly, Booknetic, LatePoint)
weaknesses: WordPress.org listing closed for a guideline violation (2025-02-01)

competitors.name: Fresha (SaaS substitute)
competitors.pricing: Independent $19.95/month; Team $14.95 per team member/month; 20% one-time marketplace commission on new clients
competitors.positioning: Software that grows with your business
strengths: Salon-specific: processing times, patch tests, packages
weaknesses: Not on your own WordPress site; marketplace commission

critic.risk: Loved, cheap alternatives already catch switchers: LatePoint (98/100, every feature at $79) and SSA (100/100, 1-day support).
Migration isn't empty: BookingPress, Sugar Calendar and PW Amelia Migration already import or move Amelia/Bookly data.
critic.rebuttal: So the angle is the done-for-you labour and a no-lost-appointments guarantee, not the importer code. Reviewers still describe being 'stuck' (e47) and a 'hostage' (e48) despite importers existing.

critic.risk: The directory is saturated: 784 results for 'appointment booking', and recent small entrants sit at 70 to 2,000 installs.
Nobody has shown they'll pay a third party to rescue or migrate a booking plugin.
WordPress.org forums forbid promoting plugins, which closes the obvious channel.
critic.rebuttal: Contact reviewers through their own published sites. Use Amelia's public r/WPAmelia and Discord within their rules, plus search content. Many reviewers are agencies (e62-e65).

critic.risk: Salons may leave WordPress booking for SaaS (Fresha $19.95/mo, Square solo tier).
At 15 h/week you can become the next 'slow support' review.
critic.rebuttal: Cap customers during the service phase, publish honest Mon-Fri hours, and ship rollback as code to cut support load.

critic.risk: Bookly's famous add-on complaint is stale (Bookly now says 'No hidden costs or add-ons'), and its low-star stream is empty for the last 12 months.
critic.rebuttal: Target Amelia first (11 low-star reviews in the last 12 months in the sample); lead with updates, support and migration, not add-on pricing.

critic.risk: WP.org guideline enforcement (BookingPress was closed for a guideline violation).
critic.rebuttal: No license kill-switches or nags; follow the plugin guidelines from day one.

I'm a WordPress developer building a booking plugin focused on rollback-safe updates and moving off Amelia/Bookly without losing appointments. I'll migrate one site free, with a before/after count you can check. No obligation, no review required.

validation.experiment: Offer a $149 done-for-you migration or rescue to people with a recent public Amelia/Bookly problem, and collect waitlist signups from two honest guides.
validation.pass_bar: 3 people agree to pay (or deposit) for a $149 migration, or 25 waitlist signups with 5 yes replies to $79/yr
steps: Day 1: buy steadyslots.com, deploy landing/index.html, build the reviewer list
Day 2: send message A to 15 reviewers via their own sites
Day 3: publish the rollback guide; answer 5 unresolved WP.org threads with no pitch
Day 4: send message B to 10 freelancers; quote $149 on jobs.wordpress.net posts
Day 5: publish the migration guide and the vs pages (with untrue promises removed)
Day 6: join r/WPAmelia and the Amelia Discord within their rules; do a timed migration dry run
Day 7: count signups, replies and paid asks; re-score willingness_to_pay

kill_criteria: Under 10 waitlist signups after 7 days and 25 direct messages
0 people willing to pay for a migration or rescue at any price you name
Most replies say they already moved to LatePoint, SSA or Fresha
Contacted reviewers say the vendor has since fixed their problem
Migration dry runs take more than 4 hours each, which breaks 15 h/week at $149
